parallel.requirements: Recognized the Node ESM .mjs port requirement, manual argv fidelity, exact print formatting, zero external dependencies, and the no Uint8Array/DataView constraint from the prompt.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent did black-box probing, owned implementation and assembly, and delegated a twelve-family verifier workflow for adversarial differential checks.
parallel.implementation: Built a layered /output/lib/bech32, /output/lib/cli, and /output/lib/python implementation plus /output/test12.mjs, then fixed a local -h=x argparse divergence.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact tree contained test12.mjs and fourteen library modules; no child-owned implementation was joined because children were verifier/audit agents.
parallel.verification: Local smoke, argparse, orchestrator, and BIP-vector checks passed, while verifier children later found argparse and repr/raw-byte mismatches that never returned as a workflow result.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The parent found a raw invalid-UTF-8/surrogateescape divergence near timeout and the verifier workflow was killed with result null, leaving known divergences unfixed.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs, manual argv, black-box executable, formatting, and dependency restrictions without using any delegation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single agent probed behavior, implemented all modules, assembled /output/test12.mjs, and performed all verification locally.
serial.implementation: Built a flatter /output/lib set and /output/test12.mjs, then fixed a convertbits pad=false bug after a differential mismatch.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered an artifact with test12.mjs and six local library modules, with no cross-agent integration boundary or subagent handoff.
serial.verification: Passed a 68-case differential suite and a 2050-case bech32 fuzz run, then found and categorized 155 argparse-surface mismatches before timeout.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out after diagnosing argparse gaps and probing double-dash behavior, so those known parsing issues were not fixed before official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the ESM, .mjs, manual argv, formatting, dependency, and forbidden API requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt obligations and also probed the executable to define exact behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition split is evidenced; both failures occurred after substantial but incomplete fidelity work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used parent-owned implementation plus a TaskCreate/Workflow verification split across twelve child fuzz families.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept probing, implementation, verification, and debugging in one local control flow with workflows disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a verifier lifecycle boundary; serial avoided cross-agent ownership and therefore had no result-return dependency.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow script supplied children with the spec path, executable, port path, diff runner, and a no-/output-modification rule.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial maintained task knowledge locally, including black-box observations and later argparse mismatch categories.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's child interface was adequate for verification, but the useful information stayed below the workflow result boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a modular bech32/cli/python implementation under nested directories and fixed a local -h=x argparse divergence.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a flatter library layout and fixed a concrete convertbits leftover-bits bug after differential testing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementations differed structurally and in which ordinary defect was fixed, but both still had unfixed argparse fidelity issues at closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel launched the verifier workflow, requested TaskOutput with blocking wait, received timeout/running, and the workflow later ended killed with result null.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial's verification results were immediate local command outputs consumed in the same trajectory, including pass counts and mismatch categories.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the major process split: parallel generated verifier findings that never returned, while serial directly consumed its local test findings.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent wrote /output artifacts and children were verifier-only, so no concrete overwrite or shared implementation collision appears.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and edited its own /output artifacts locally, with no subagent workspace sharing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No retained shared-state failure separates the runs; the parallel issue is result lifecycle rather than write collision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel local checks passed many suites, but workflow children found argparse and repr/raw-byte divergences that did not reach the parent as a result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial passed 68 direct cases and 2050 bech32 fuzz cases, then found and categorized 155 argparse mismatches locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more concurrent verification breadth, but serial's verification findings were available to the main actor without a workflow return barrier.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after 2401 seconds with twelve subagents and a killed workflow; the parent was still investigating raw-byte divergence.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out after 2400 seconds, but with zero workflow calls/subagents and local argparse diagnosis still unfinished.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both closed under timeout and both failed officially, but only parallel lost actionable child verifier findings behind an unfinished workflow.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status/evaluation records show both runs failed officially with the same 3/70 pass count, so there is no discordant official outcome. The concrete task-solving difference is procedural: parallel used a broad verifier workflow whose findings did not return before timeout, while serial consumed all verification locally and reached an argparse diagnosis before timing out.
parallel_contributors: Verifier workflow findings did not return to the parent before closure.
The parent found an additional raw invalid-UTF-8/surrogateescape divergence near timeout.
serial_contributors: Serial consumed its local verification output directly, including 68-case and 2050-case pass results.
Serial locally categorized 155 argparse mismatches before timing out.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel fixed a -h=x argparse class but still had repr/raw-byte and other argparse fidelity issues.
Serial fixed convertbits after a mismatch but left known argparse classes unresolved.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel adverse process event, not an official outcome explanation

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly owned implementation and created the /output ESM library and entry point; missing ownership is not the observed failure.
The parent integrated its own modules and final entry point, and no incompatible independently owned implementation components required an absent integrator.
The deliverable /output/test12.mjs was assembled by the parent; the failure was not absence of an assembly owner.
The parent owned the end-to-end pipeline, including probing, implementation, local tests, workflow verification, and closure checks.
Implementation was not blocked behind a single mandatory serial preflight; probing, implementation, and later workflow verification all occurred.
The parallel run did not complete all investigation as a separate first phase before productive work; it wrote the implementation before launching the verifier workflow.
Although the run timed out, the indispensable implementation path was actively owned by the parent; the direct retained boundary is missing verifier return.
The verifier workflow was broad, but the concrete adverse event is that child findings existed and never returned; breadth alone is not retained as the direct boundary.
No single child assignment is the directly evidenced overbroad unit; the children were family-specific verifiers and the retained issue is aggregate result non-return.
The workflow brief included the task, /output paths, executable, no-output-write rule, and differential acceptance requirements; children followed it.
Verifier children were not separately producing interoperating implementation components, and their corpus/result contract was specified in the workflow script.
There is no transfer where known information was omitted or truncated before reaching a receiver; the key findings did not return at all.
No completed large handoff reached the parent and then went unconsumed due to volume; the workflow aggregate result was absent.
The parent did not act on a superseded returned report; the verifier result never returned before closure.
No incompatible completed reports reached the parent and remained unadjudicated; the available child findings were below the workflow boundary.
The parent did not present the whole task as complete; it was still checking and had found a raw-byte divergence when the process timed out.
There was no replacement child or retry that repeated prior work without inherited findings; the workflow remained in its original run.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The workflow was killed at run closure, but the more specific observed boundary is that verifier findings existed yet never returned as a workflow result.
No complete, directly promotable final candidate with all known divergences fixed existed; the parent had just found another mismatch before timeout.
No child implementation change was merged after integrated verification; the workflow children were verifiers and no post-verification merge occurred.
The delegated work was verification, not a completed implementation waiting to be adopted into the final artifact.

The parallel parent launched a verifier workflow and later attempted a blocking TaskOutput, but it received only a timeout/running status. Inside the workflow, verifier children had already produced concrete differential findings, including argparse and repr-path mismatches, yet the workflow state at closure had status killed and result null. Those actionable verifier findings therefore never returned to the parent before closure.
candidates.realized_consequence: Actionable verifier findings about argparse Unicode/negative-number handling and Python repr/raw-byte behavior remained trapped below the workflow boundary and were not incorporated into the parent implementation before timeout.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent did not simply wait without inspection: it called TaskOutput, received a running timeout, and continued local checks. The sharper boundary is the verifier findings not returning from the workflow.

candidates.reason: The parent received a running/timeout status rather than a concrete child failure to take over; the same chain is captured by missing verifier return.
The parent did not receive a completed verifier result and ignore it; the completed findings were not returned to the parent.
The parent did inspect the workflow with TaskOutput and continued local checks afterward, so this was not waiting without inspection.
Verifier children were instructed not to modify /output and no competing implementation paths requiring reconciliation are evidenced.
No live agents edited the same source file with observed reconciliation or collision.
No child or parent replacement of another actor's non-entry source is evidenced.
No concurrent actor overwrote the submitted entry point while another actor owned or used it.
No broad cleanup or promotion replaced multiple final outputs and invalidated another actor's work.
The workflow children operated as verifiers and no concrete unstable shared-workspace provenance problem is evidenced.
No generated artifact from one concurrent actor was consumed by another as a mistaken reference environment.
